recipes.name: Butter Lamb Gravy
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 1 inch pieces
0.5 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Season the lamb with garam masala and salt. Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Fry the lamb cubes until browned, stirring constantly. Remove from the skillet and set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the same skillet over medium heat. Add the onion; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes.

Stir in the turmeric, ginger, and garlic. Cook and stir for 1 minute. Stir in the cayenne and tomato paste until well blended, then stir in the water. Bring to a simmer and return lamb to the skillet. Simmer over low heat for about 20 minutes, or until lamb is tender.
Stir in the cream and honey. Transfer to a serving dish and garnish with cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: Butter Lamb Gravy
raw_recipe.description: Lamb is simmered in a spicy tomato curry enriched with cream. This is a very mouthwatering dish that is easy to make. Serve with hot cooked rice or your favorite bread.

review.reviewBody: I can't imagine why this recipe doesn't have more positive ratings!!! Firstly my local grocery store didn't have garam masala so I made my own : 2 cinnamon sticks 3 dried bay leaves 3 tbsp cumin seeds 2 tbsp coriander seeds 4 cardamom pods, crushed 1 tbsp cloves 1 tsp black peppercorns 1 tbsp ground mace Dry roast the ingredients, let cool and grind to a fine powder(you can use spice mill or coffee grinder). Store in the pantry for up to 1 month and in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. I also didn't have any creme fraiche so I used heavy whipping cream and one word for this : YUMMY!!!My boyfriend and I could not get enough of this!! Please try this you will not regret it!!!!

This was good, but not outanding. I would recommend doubling the spices for sure. I did not have creme fraiche, so I used 1/4c. sour cream and 1/4 C half & half instead. After browing the lamb, I drained off all but 2T of the fat, but then as it cooked, there wasn't enough liquid. I added more cream to compensate. After tasting about 1/2 way through, I added salt, another Tbsp of tomato paste. It definitely improved after adding the honey, cream & cilantro to finish. Don't leave any of those out. The end product was tasty, but I'll tweak it with add'l spice next time and maybe use chicken or shrimp.

I loved this recipe so much I counted stop eating it! I did a few variations because I didn't have heavy cream and I used sour cream. Also I cooked it in a cast iron skillet and placed it in the oven on a slow bake of 275 for about an hour. Delish!!!

This dish as per the recipe is very bland. So on my second attempt I made a few changes: 1. I added 1 tbs of ginger and garlic which I pounded together in a mortar; 3 green cardamoms; 3 tbs tomato paste; 1 green chilli sliced; double the Garam masala (which I made myself, minus the nutmeg); the suggested amount of turmeric; 1/4 cup whipping cream; and no honey; salt to taste 2. After I browned the meat, I removed it from the pot, then sautéed the ginger garlic and green cardamom together until the garlic was light brown in 1tbs butter and 1 tbs oil. 3. I added the meat back to the pot and cooked as per the recipe. 4. I also added 1tbs butter when I added the cream. The flavours were a lot more robust and my family loved it.

This recipe is amazing! I've made it twice so far - first time with pork, second time with chicken - and loved it! Next time I make it with pork, I'll reduce the cooking time, since the pork turned out a little dry - but the sauce made up for it, no worries. The chicken turned out perfect - I can't wait to make it with lamb! I also doubled the amount of tomato paste. Instead of water and creme fresh I only used one glass of 1% fat milk. The taste is just as great! I also used more of the spices for taste and added about one teaspoon coriander powder. Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe, it's a keeper!

This recipe is amazing!! I left out the cayenne pepper so my family would eat it, and they loved it!! 
I took the lamb and put it in a covered bowl with a thickly chopped onion, and some sea salt. Then I put it in the fridge for three days stirring twice a day. Lamb was so tender!
Like I said, recipe is so good that I'll never eat butter anything in a restaurant ever again!
Thanks!! :)

Loved the recipe. Had to make it the second time. The first time I cooked it I followed the recipe and it didn’t come out nice. I was using leg of lamb cubes and they were hard and chewy. I doubled up all the spices and even water this time around. Cooked the leg of lamb on low heat for 3hrs. Absolute perfection

Never cooked this kind of food before. Followed the recipe exactly. This turned out great! I was worried about it being too thin of a sauce so I cooked it a little longer on medium after adding cream. The sauce thickened nice after cooling a bit. It has a fair amount of heat but well balanced. I trimmed the lamb of all the fat I could and it was still tender. Just make sure to remove with just a brown and dont try and cook it done at the beginning. Served with basmati rice. Simple enough to throw together on a workday. Highly recommend!!

7/15/16 Update - made this using 2 lbs of cremini and baby bella mushrooms in place of the lamb. This butter gravy sauce is so good. I am not a huge vegetarian dish lover so would ultimately still prefer the lamb over mushrooms but my wife loved the veggie dinner. I can't wait to try this on other meats!

Most pleasant. Quick and easy to prepare. I had stewing lamb meat and was looking for something different. I saw this one, and just let it simmer longer for the meat to become tender. I used chillies instead of powder. I was extremely wary of the amount of honey. For my taste, I found 1/2 tbsp. quite enough. But that is like salt and pepper - a personal taste.

I increased by 2x's most of the spices (3 tbsp of GM), increased the butter to 3 tbsp, used 3/4 cups of water. 

Used left over lamb shoulder from a roast. (it was a big roast).

With the changes I made it gets a 4. 

I enjoyed it, my 9 year old son loved it and had seconds. The others wished it wasn't lamb ;)

This is a good recipe--and with a few changes it is amazing. I like a little more sauce with a little more flavor, so I doubled everything except the meat and garam masala. Keep the meat quantity as it is and quadruple the garam masala (2 tsp. total). With those tweaks, this recipe was very much like the curries I used to eat in England!
This is amazing
Tastes great and family requests it often. I did increase the spices some to give it a little more kick and flavour.

This sauce was so good I kept thinking about wanting to add more things to the mix - like potatoes, vegetables, etc. Purists might not be happy with the lack of toasted spices and authentic methods, but I really liked it, and I liked that it was way less greasy/oily than most restaurant versions. Scales down by half well.
Delicious!!
Triple garam masala and garlic. Double tumeric and ginger. Cayenne stays the same.
I made this with leftover roast lamb. I added some potato and peas because that's how I like my curries. Served it over steamed rice. Very tasty.
My husband and I both like Indian food, and in addition to being delicious, this dish is easy to prepare. I’m adding it to my list of recipes!

The flavor is good though I did have to add some salt to my portion. When I make this again, I shall do it in the slow cooker though as the meat stayed pretty chewy after only 20 minutes of simmering.
